stories.title: Amazon’s AI assistant can now spot fake emails from the company
stories.simple_summary: Amazon has added a tool to its Alexa assistant that can check whether an email or text message really came from Amazon, helping you spot fake messages trying to trick you into giving away information.
stories.why_it_matters: If you shop on Amazon and get suspicious messages, this tool could help you avoid scams — though you'll still need to be careful and think before clicking anything.

stories.title: Pangram’s Max Spero on why AI detection is harder than ‘Real or Fake’
stories.simple_summary: Companies are struggling to tell the difference between real and fake content on the internet, because AI can now create convincing fake text and images that look real enough to fool people.
stories.why_it_matters: This matters because you might accidentally believe fake reviews about products, or businesses might get fooled by fake job applications — it's getting harder to know what's genuine.

stories.title: We’re ‘dangerously close’ to dead internet theory, says Pangram’s CEO
stories.simple_summary: Some experts worry the internet is becoming so full of AI-generated junk content that soon you won't be able to trust whether anything you read is real or made by a computer.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a concern for the future of the internet, but right now it's mostly a problem computer scientists are thinking about — nothing you need to act on immediately.

stories.title: US government sides with OpenAI on issue of training LLMs on copyrighted material
stories.simple_summary: The U.S. government said it's okay for companies like OpenAI to use copyrighted material (like newspaper articles) to teach their AI systems, rather than having to pay for permission.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and big tech companies — it affects whether AI companies can grow faster, but nothing you need to worry about in your daily life.

stories.title: Researchers fear safety disaster ahead of OpenAI’s Astra release
stories.simple_summary: OpenAI is about to release a powerful new AI system, but researchers are worried it could be dangerous because it acted unpredictably during testing.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly a concern for tech experts and safety researchers — if you're not using OpenAI's advanced tools for work, this doesn't affect you yet.

stories.title: Kids go from curious to frustrated playing with AI-stuffed toys, UW study finds
stories.simple_summary: A study found that children start out excited to play with toy robots that use AI, but quickly get frustrated when the toys don't work the way they expect.
stories.why_it_matters: If you're buying AI toys for grandchildren, this suggests they might get bored quickly — like any toy, the novelty wears off fast.

stories.title: The Trump administration is supporting OpenAI in the NYT copyright lawsuit
stories.simple_summary: The Trump administration took OpenAI's side in a lawsuit where the New York Times is claiming OpenAI used its articles without permission to train its AI.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to publishers and tech investors — it affects how companies can use news articles, but nothing affecting your daily life right now.

stories.title: Wonderful more than doubles its valuation to $5B in under 6 months
stories.simple_summary: A company called Wonderful became worth $5 billion (double what it was six months ago) after raising $550 million in investment money.
stories.why_it_matters: This is investor news — it doesn't affect regular people or small businesses unless you're thinking about investing in tech startups.

stories.title: India’s richest man now wants to turn aging computers into AI-ready PCs
stories.simple_summary: An Indian company wants to upgrade old computers to work with AI tools for very cheap, around $11 for two months of service.
stories.why_it_matters: If you have an old computer sitting around, this might eventually be a cheap way to make it useful for AI tasks, but this is mostly being developed for India right now.

stories.title: Tencent-backed Enflame IPO draws 6,109 times online demand
stories.simple_summary: A Chinese company called Enflame is going public and getting huge investor interest in buying shares.
stories.why_it_matters: This is investment news — it only matters if you own stocks or are interested in tech company valuations.

stories.title: Google is sending MrBeast into the wilderness, armed with AI
stories.simple_summary: Google paid a popular YouTuber named MrBeast to use Google's AI assistant and other Google products in his videos.
stories.why_it_matters: This doesn't affect you unless you watch MrBeast videos — it's basically an advertisement disguised as entertainment.

stories.title: Brazil’s electoral court sets new standards for AI deepfakes after case involving Sen. Bolsonaro
stories.simple_summary: Brazil's courts created new rules to stop people from using AI to create fake videos of politicians and election candidates.
stories.why_it_matters: This is important for protecting elections from misinformation, but it mostly matters if you live in Brazil or follow Brazilian politics.
